intro.title: Discover The Great Arch of the Defense
intro.description:
The Great Arch of the Defense (La Grande Arche de la Défense), also known as the 'Modern Arc de Triomphe', is one of France's most iconic modern architectural masterpieces. Designed by Danish architect Johan Otto von Spreckelsen, it was completed in 1989 to commemorate the 200th anniversary of the French Revolution.

This magnificent white marble structure stands 110 meters high, 110 meters wide, and 110 meters deep, forming a massive cubic 'arch'. It perfectly aligns with Paris's historical axis—from the Louvre Pyramid, through the Champs-Élysées, to the Arc de Triomphe, and finally to La Grande Arche.

The Arche is not just an architectural masterpiece but also a multifunctional space containing office areas, exhibition spaces, and an observation deck at the top. From the deck, visitors can enjoy 360-degree panoramic views of Paris, including the iconic historical axis.

As the centerpiece of the La Défense business district, this monument symbolizes France's modernization and vision for the future while maintaining respect for history and tradition.

knowledge.title: The Story of The Great Arch

sections.title: History & Construction
sections.content:
The Great Arch of the Defense project began in 1982 as part of France's 'Grands Travaux' (Great Works) program initiated by President François Mitterrand. The goal was to create a modern triumphal arch perfectly aligned with Paris's historical axis.

Danish architect Johan Otto von Spreckelsen won the international design competition in 1983. His design was a massive white marble cube with a hollowed center forming an 'arch'. The official inauguration took place on July 14, 1989, coinciding with the 200th anniversary of the French Revolution.

sections.title: Architectural Significance
sections.content:
La Grande Arche is not just a building but a symbol. It represents France's vision for the future while maintaining respect for history and tradition. The structure's pure lines and monumental scale embody modernist ideals.

The location of the Arche is deeply meaningful—it sits at the western end of Paris's historical axis, which begins at the Louvre, continues through the Tuileries Garden, Champs-Élysées, Arc de Triomphe, and finally reaches La Défense. This spatial arrangement reflects France's continuity from history to modernity.

sections.title: Architectural Features
sections.content:
La Grande Arche is an astounding engineering feat:

1. Dimensions: 110m high, 110m wide, 110m deep—a perfect cube
2. Materials: White Carrara marble, glass, and steel
3. Weight: Approximately 300,000 tons
4. Design: Hollow cube forming a 'gate' shape
5. Observation deck: Open-air deck at the top, accommodating hundreds

The north and south wings of the building are enclosed office spaces, while the east and west faces are open 'arches'. This design is both functional and rich in symbolism.

sections.title: About the Architect
sections.content:
Johan Otto von Spreckelsen (1929-1987) was a renowned Danish architect and designer. He was known for his minimalist and classical modernist style.

Other notable works by Spreckelsen include St. Bernard's Church in Copenhagen. His design philosophy emphasized pure geometric forms, high-quality materials, and careful handling of light. Unfortunately, Spreckelsen passed away in 1987 and did not live to see the completion of the Grande Arche. The project was completed by French architect Paul Andreu.

transport.title: How to Get Here
transport.fromCenterDesc: Take Metro Line 1 from Arc de Triomphe, get off at 'La Défense - Grande Arche' station. Journey takes about 10 minutes. This is the most convenient transport option.
transport.fromStationDesc: Take Metro Line 4 then transfer to Line 1, get off at 'La Défense - Grande Arche' station. Total journey about 30 minutes.
transport.publicTransportDesc:
Metro Line 1: Terminal station 'La Défense - Grande Arche'
RER A: 'La Défense' station
Bus: Multiple lines serve La Défense
transport.walkingDesc: La Défense district itself is an open-air architecture museum, perfect for walking tours of numerous modern architectural masterpieces.
transport.drivingDesc: Multiple underground parking lots available in La Défense district. However, public transport is recommended for convenience and environmental reasons.

route.title: Recommended Itinerary
route.overview: Start from Arc de Triomphe, take Metro Line 1 to La Grande Arche (10 minutes), visit the Arche and observation deck (1.5 hours), enjoy panoramic views of Paris from the top, then explore La Défense modern architecture district (1 hour). Total trip takes about half a day.
steps: Start at Arc de Triomphe, take Metro Line 1 at 'Charles de Gaulle - Étoile' station
Get off at 'La Défense - Grande Arche' station, follow signs to the Grande Arche
Visit the base of the Arche, admire the monumental scale and white marble facade
Take the elevator to the top observation deck, enjoy 360-degree panoramic views of Paris
From the deck, identify Paris's historical axis: Arc de Triomphe, Champs-Élysées, Louvre
Visit exhibition spaces inside the Arche (if available)
Exit the Arche, explore other modern buildings in La Défense district
Visit the nearby 'Le Delta' and La Défense Plaza
Choose from numerous restaurants in La Défense for lunch or dinner
Take the Metro back to Paris city center, or enjoy the night view of the Arche at dusk

officialManagement.title: About The Great Arch of the Defense
officialManagement.text:
The Great Arch of the Defense (La Grande Arche de la Défense) is one of France's most iconic modern architectural masterpieces, designed by Danish architect Johan Otto von Spreckelsen and completed in 1989 to commemorate the 200th anniversary of the French Revolution.

This magnificent white marble structure is located at the heart of Paris's La Défense business district, perfectly aligned with the historical axis from the Louvre to the Arc de Triomphe. The Grande Arche is not just an architectural masterpiece but also features an observation deck offering visitors 360-degree panoramic views of Paris.
